what_its_for: Everolimus is used to treat certain types of cancer (such as kidney cancer, breast cancer, and certain brain or pancreatic tumors) and to prevent your body from rejecting a transplanted organ (kidney or liver). It works by slowing down the growth of cancer cells or calming the immune system so it does not attack the new organ.
how_to_take: Take everolimus by mouth, with or without food, but try to take it the same way every time (always with food or always without food). Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. If you are using the dispersible tablet (Afinitor Disperz), dissolve it in water as instructed by your pharmacist — do not swallow it whole. Take it at the same time every day. Drink plenty of water unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Wash your hands before and after handling the tablets.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, body size, and other medicines you take. The usual dose for cancer treatment is 10 mg once daily. For transplant patients, the dose is lower and is based on blood levels that your doctor monitors regularly. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 6 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 6 hours, skip the missed dose completely and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store everolimus tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the tablets in their original package or container and protect them from light. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and cause serious side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), as it can make everolimus less effective. Avoid live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu spray) while taking this medicine — talk to your doctor before getting any shots. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Avoid getting cuts or injuries without protecting the area. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should avoid handling crushed or broken tablets.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: trouble breathing or shortness of breath, a new or worsening cough, fever, chills, or signs of infection, mouth sores or pain when swallowing, unusual swelling of your legs, ankles, or feet, chest pain, signs of high blood sugar (increased thirst, frequent urination, blurry vision), signs of kidney problems (decreased urination, swelling), unusual bleeding or bruising, extreme tiredness or weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or any new or unusual symptoms. These could be signs of serious side effects that need prompt medical attention.
when_it_works: Everolimus starts working in your body right away, but you may not notice any changes immediately. For cancer treatment, it may take several weeks to months before your doctor can tell if the medicine is working through scans or tests. For transplant patients, the medicine begins protecting your new organ right away. Do not stop taking it just because you feel well — it is important to keep taking it as directed.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to side effects, especially infections and mouth sores. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: Afinitor Disperz is approved for certain children with specific brain tumors. Dosing is based on body size and must be determined by a doctor. Pregnancy: Do NOT take everolimus if you are pregnant, as it can harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 8 weeks after your last dose. Both men and women should use contraception. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 2 weeks after stopping. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have liver problems. Let your doctor know about all health conditions before starting this medicine.
